newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk Migros sees 40 pct real growth in 1996 sales.
newsitem.headline: Turk Migros sees 40 pct real growth in 1996 sales.

text.p: Turkish supermarket chain Migros Turk T.A.S. is expecting a 40 percent real growth in sales this year and planning to sustain annual growth of 20 percent over the next three years, a senior firm official said.

"Our annual growth target is 20 percent in real terms until the new century, according to the basic principles of our year 2000 strategies," Migros general manager Bulent Ozaydinli told Reuters in an interview.
Total sales of Migros in the first half of the year soared to 18.09 trillion lira against 7.25 trillion lira in the same 1995 period and 19.31 trillion in the whole of 1995.
Its first half net profits were 558.2 billion lira, up 85 percent from a year ago, compared to a year-on-year consumer inflation of 82.9 percent in June.
Ozaydinli said the company achieved a 20 percent real annual sales growth between 1990-1993 and 30 percent between 1993-1995.

"The aim of Migros for the year 2000 is to be shown among the big European chains and to achieve total sales figures spelled in billion-dollar terms. We do not limit our targets with the borders of Turkey, we expand them to European measures," he said.
The shares of the company closed steady at 69,000 lira on Monday morning.
Migros has introduced a new retailer chain, "Shock", whose sales points were set up in low-middle income districts. Migros stores are located in middle and high-middle income districts.

The company operates 34 Shock stores and 68 supermarkets. It has opened 27 new stores this year and is planning to open 23 others this year in various towns, including southeastern Diyarbakir and eastern Erzurum.
The company has plans to set up supermarket chains in the former Soviet states and Romania.
"We will take the advantage of being first in a market where there is no western competitor," Ozaydinli said.
Migros has already opened a store in the Azeri capital of Baku.
Migros recently faced competition in the domestic market from many new companies including French Carrefour and German Metro. -- Istanbul newsroom +90-212-2750875.
